angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 276,889 km at 56.91 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.5716 +/- 0.0110 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 56.91 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.398 +/- 0.012 solar radii from Cointepas et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-269 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract): 276,889 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.3917 +/- 0.0095 solar masses from Cointepas et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-269 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3514 +/- 70 K from Cointepas et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-269 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cointepas et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-269 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-269.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.831, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-269 (pscomppars): spectral type M2 V, from Cointepas et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, TOI-269: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-269 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.29 dex, from Cointepas et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...650A.145C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-269 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.64675, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/MNRAS/520/5283/table1 (Rotation periods and ages of cool host stars), column Prot: 35.7 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place
